name: Extramedullary Soft Tissue Plasmacytoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: International Myeloma Working Group Criteria for Extramedullary Plasmacytoma

criteria.description: Histopathological confirmation of monoclonal plasma cell infiltration in soft tissue mass
No or minimal (<10%) clonal plasma cells in bone marrow aspirate
No evidence of multiple myeloma or multiple bone lesions on imaging
Absent or low serum and urine monoclonal protein levels

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus absence of bone marrow involvement and multiple lesions
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of systemic multiple myeloma and confirmation of localized plasma cell tumor in soft tissue.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized soft tissue mass with monoclonal plasma cell infiltration
pathognomonic.notes: Typically presents as a solitary, painless mass
searchTerms: localized soft tissue tumor with plasma cells
soft tissue swelling with immune cell infiltration

pathognomonic.symptomName: Monoclonal protein spike absent or minimal in serum electrophoresis
searchTerms: no or low abnormal protein in blood test

common.symptomName: Soft tissue mass causing local compression symptoms
common.notes: May cause functional impairment depending on location
searchTerms: soft tissue mass pressing on nearby structures

occasional.symptomName: Local pain or tenderness at tumor site
occasional.notes: May occur if mass compresses nerves or tissues
searchTerms: pain or tenderness at tumor site

occasional.symptomName: Mild constitutional symptoms such as low-grade fever
searchTerms: mild general symptoms like low-grade fever

occasional.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to nerve compression

rare.symptomName: Pathological fracture due to bone involvement
rare.notes: Rare, suggests progression to multiple myeloma

laboratory: Serum protein electrophoresis showing absent or low monoclonal protein
Bone marrow biopsy with <10% plasma cells
Elevated ESR and beta-2 microglobulin in some cases
imaging: MRI or CT showing solitary soft tissue mass without bone involvement
Skeletal survey negative for lytic bone lesions
genetic: Clonal plasma cell population with immunoglobulin light chain restriction
No specific recurrent genetic mutations identified
other: Histopathology demonstrating monoclonal plasma cells with immunohistochemistry positive for CD138 and light chain restriction

distinguishingFeatures: Higher bone marrow plasma cell infiltration (>10%)
Significant monoclonal protein in serum and urine
Lesion located within bone rather than soft tissue
Presence of lymphadenopathy and bone marrow involvement

redFlags: Neurological deficits due to nerve compression
Signs of systemic involvement such as anemia, hypercalcemia, or renal failure
references: International Myeloma Working Group. Criteria for diagnosis of extramedullary plasmacytoma. Leukemia. 2014.
Orphanet: Extramedullary Soft Tissue Plasmacytoma. ORPHA:100022.
Kyle RA, Rajkumar SV. Plasma cell disorders. Lancet. 2004.
